about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Pikelets with Apricot Jam
recipes.summary: Small fluffy griddle cakes, an old Australian morning-tea favourite, served with jam.
steps: Mix the flour and sugar in a bowl. Whisk the egg, milk and butter, then stir into the flour until just smooth, with no big lumps.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and grease lightly. Drop in tablespoons of batter and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until bubbles form and burst on top.
Flip and cook for 1 minute more, until golden. Repeat to make 24 pikelets and serve with the apricot jam.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 pikelets with 1 tsp jam. Best warm; keeps 2 days in the fridge and freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and cook the pikelets until the centres are no longer wet.

recipes.title: Honey Joys
recipes.summary: Crunchy corn flake clusters in a buttery honey coating, baked in patty cases.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and set 24 mini paper cases in a mini muffin tin.
Melt the butter, sugar and honey in a saucepan over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Pour over the corn flakes and fold gently until evenly coated.
Spoon into the cases and bake for 12 minutes, until set and golden. Cool in the tin.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 honey joys. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

recipes.title: Chocolate Crackles
recipes.summary: No-bake rice bubble and cocoa treats set with coconut oil, a party classic.
steps: Mix the puffed rice, sifted icing sugar, cocoa and coconut in a large bowl.
Pour in the cooled coconut oil and stir until every piece is coated and the mix holds together.
Spoon into 24 paper cases and refrigerate until firm.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackles. Keeps 1 week in the fridge; they soften in warm weather.

recipes.title: Chocolate Oat Fingers
recipes.summary: A baked cocoa oat slice with a melted chocolate topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Mix the oats, flour, cocoa and sugar.
Stir in the butter and egg to a crumbly dough, press firmly into the tin and bake for 20 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Scatter the chocolate over the hot slice, leave for 3 minutes and spread smooth. Cool and cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until the slice is firm and golden.

recipes.title: Afghan Biscuits
recipes.summary: New Zealand-style chocolate cornflake biscuits topped with chocolate icing and a walnut.

items: 1 tbsp cocoa powder, for the icing

steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then stir in the flour and cocoa, then gently fold in the corn flakes.
Roll into 12 balls, place 5cm apart on the trays and flatten gently with a fork. Bake for 15 minutes, until firm. Cool on the tray.
Stir the icing sugar, icing cocoa, icing butter and 1 tbsp hot water until smooth and spreadable. Ice each biscuit and top with a walnut half.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 biscuit. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts.

recipes.title: Lamington Bites
recipes.summary: Bite-sized sponge cubes dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in coconut.
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C fan (195°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Whisk the eggs and sugar for 6 minutes until thick and tripled in volume. Fold in the sifted flour, then the butter and milk.
Pour into the tin and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and springy to the touch. Cool completely, then cut into 12 cubes.
Whisk the icing sugar, cocoa, icing butter and icing milk in a bowl over a pan of simmering water until smooth. Dip the cubes in the icing, then roll in the coconut and set on a rack.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 lamington bite. Best within 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until the sponge springs back and a skewer comes out clean.

recipes.title: Vanilla Slice Squares
recipes.summary: Crisp puff pastry layers around thick vanilla custard and a white icing top.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Place the pastry sheets on lined trays, prick with a fork, top each with another tray and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool.
Whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour with a splash of the milk. Heat the rest of the milk until steaming, whisk into the yolk mix and return to the pan.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, whisking constantly, until thick and bubbling. Off the heat, stir in the butter and vanilla and cool for 15 minutes.

Lay one pastry sheet in a lined 20cm square tin, spread with the custard, then top with the second sheet. Mix the icing sugar with 2 tbsp water, spread over the top, then chill until the custard is firm. Cut into 12 squares with a serrated knife.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Best within 2 days, kept in the fridge.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, cook the custard until thick and bubbling, and keep refrigerated.

recipes.title: Ginger Nut Biscuits
recipes.summary: Crunchy golden syrup and ginger biscuits for dunking.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flour, sugar, ginger and bicarbonate of soda.
Melt the butter and golden syrup in a small pan for 2 minutes, then stir into the dry mix to form a firm dough.
Roll into 24 balls, place 5cm apart on the trays and bake for 15 minutes, until deep golden. Cool on the tray, where they firm up and crisp.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Tray Baked Granola Clusters
recipes.summary: Big crunchy oat and almond clusters sweetened with maple syrup.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a large tray with baking paper.
Mix the oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds and coconut. Stir the maple syrup and coconut oil together, pour over and mix until every piece is glossy.
Spread out and press down firmly. Bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden, then cool completely without stirring so it sets in clusters. Break up and stir through the raisins.
notes: Snack. Per serving: about 1/2 cup (45g). Keeps 3 weeks in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Glazed Almonds
recipes.summary: Crisp sugar-and-cinnamon coated almonds, baked low and slow.
steps: Heat the oven to 140°C fan (160°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Whisk the egg white until frothy, 1 minute.
Mix the sugar, cinnamon and salt, then toss the almonds in the egg white and then in the sugar mix.
Spread on the tray and bake for 35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until dry and fragrant. Cool completely to crisp.
notes: Snack. Per serving: a small handful (35g). Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and wash your hands after handling it. The low oven fully dries the coating.

recipes.title: Apple Sultana Lunchbox Muffins
recipes.summary: Lightly sweet apple and sultana muffins that freeze well for school lunchboxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, sugar and cinnamon. Whisk the egg, milk and oil, pour into the dry mix with the apple and sultanas and stir until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and bake until a skewer comes out clean.

recipes.title: Zucchini Mozzarella Muffins
recipes.summary: Savoury muffins with grated zucchini, melty mozzarella and chives.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil. Stir into the flour with the zucchini, mozzarella and chives until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months and reheat at 160°C fan for 8 minutes.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Hummus Veggie Pinwheels
recipes.summary: Soft tortilla rolls spread with hummus and packed with carrot, cucumber and spinach.
steps: Spread each tortilla edge to edge with the hummus.
Cover with the spinach, carrot and cucumber, leaving a 2cm border at one end.
Roll up tightly from the other end, wrap in baking paper and chill until firm enough to slice cleanly, then cut each roll into 6 pinwheels.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 4 pinwheels. Keeps 1 day in the fridge in an airtight container, so make them the morning you serve them.

recipes.title: Spanakopita Bites
recipes.summary: Crisp filo triangles filled with spinach, feta and ricotta.

items: 300g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the spinach, feta, ricotta, egg and nutmeg.

Cut the stacked filo into 3 strips each, lengthways, and keep covered with a damp tea towel. Brush a strip with oil, put 1 tbsp of filling at one end and fold over and over like a flag into a triangle. Repeat to make 12 triangles.
Place seam side down on the trays, brush with the remaining oil and bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 triangle. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat at 180°C fan for 8 minutes to crisp.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg, bake until golden and hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Bacon and Cheese Pastry Cups
recipes.summary: Buttery pastry cases filled with bacon, mozzarella and a soft egg custard.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Cut 12 rounds from the pastry and press into the holes.
Fry the bacon in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp. Divide the bacon and mozzarella among the cases.
Whisk the eggs, cream, nutmeg and pepper, pour over and bake for 22 minutes, until puffed, golden and just set in the centre.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes before turning out.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 pastry cups. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat at 170°C fan for 10 minutes.

Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the filling until it reaches at least 70°C and the custard is set, use fresh, uncracked eggs and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Cheesy Ham Egg Cups
recipes.summary: Baked egg muffins with ham, capsicum, spring onion and mozzarella, high in protein.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin well.
Divide the ham, capsicum, spring onions and mozzarella among the holes. Whisk the eggs, milk and pepper and pour over.
Bake for 18 minutes, until puffed and set in the centre. Cool in the tin for 3 minutes before lifting out.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 egg cups. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 1 month and reheat in the microwave for 1 minute.

Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until the egg is firm and the centres reach at least 70°C, keep the ham refrigerated until use and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Pizza Muffins
recipes.summary: Savoury muffins with tomato paste, ham and mozzarella, a lunchbox favourite.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk the egg, milk, oil and tomato paste. Stir into the flour with the ham, three-quarters of the mozzarella and the oregano until just combined.
Divide among the cases, top with the remaining mozzarella and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg, keep the ham refrigerated until use, bake until hot throughout and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.title: Baked Pumpkin Chickpea Nuggets
recipes.summary: Crisp-edged nuggets of roasted pumpkin and chickpeas with breadcrumbs and cumin.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp of the oil for 20 minutes, until soft and golden.
Mash the pumpkin and chickpeas roughly with a fork, then mix in the egg, half the breadcrumbs, cumin and salt. Shape into 24 nuggets and coat in the remaining breadcrumbs.
Brush with the remaining oil and bake on the tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 nuggets. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months and reheat at 180°C fan for 12 minutes.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and bake until hot throughout. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Pear Oat Bars
recipes.summary: Crumbly oat bars layered with softened cinnamon pear.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Simmer the pear, cinnamon and lemon juice in a pan with 2 tbsp water for 6 minutes until soft.
Mix the oats, flour, sugar and butter. Press two-thirds into the tin and bake for 10 minutes.
Spread the pear over the base, crumble over the remaining oat mix and bake for 20 minutes, until golden. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

recipes.title: Marmalade Oat Biscuits
recipes.summary: Chewy oat biscuits with a bittersweet orange marmalade note.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the egg and marmalade.
Stir in the flour, oats and bicarbonate of soda to form a firm dough. Roll into 24 balls and flatten slightly on the trays, 4cm apart.
Bake for 14 minutes, until golden at the edges. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and bake until golden.

recipes.title: Chocolate Coconut Rough
recipes.summary: Dark chocolate clusters with coconut, raisins and almonds, no baking.
steps: Melt the chocolate in a bowl over barely simmering water for 5 minutes, stirring, until smooth.
Stir in the coconut, raisins and almonds until everything is coated.
Drop 12 heaped spoonfuls onto a lined tray and refrigerate until firm.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cluster. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge. Contains tree nuts.

recipes.title: Honey Rice Bubble Bars
recipes.summary: Chewy puffed rice bars set with butter, honey and brown sugar.
steps: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Melt the butter, honey and sugar in a saucepan over low heat for 4 minutes, stirring, until smooth, then boil gently for 1 minute until bubbling.
Pour over the puffed rice and sultanas and fold until coated.
Press firmly into the tin, chill until firm and cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

recipes.title: Carrot Raisin Lunchbox Loaf
recipes.summary: A moist spiced loaf with carrot and raisins, sliced for lunchboxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 10 x 21cm loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil until smooth, stir in the carrot and raisins, then fold in the flour and cinnamon.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes and cut into 12 slices.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 slice. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze slices for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until a skewer comes out clean.

recipes.title: Fudgy Kumara Brownies
recipes.summary: Rich chocolate brownies made fudgy with mashed sweet potato and almond meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Boil the sweet potato for 12 minutes until soft, then drain and mash until smooth.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over barely simmering water for 4 minutes until smooth, then stir in the sweet potato, cocoa and sugar. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the almond meal.
Spread into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until set with a few moist crumbs on a skewer. Cool and cut into 12 squares.
notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 brownie. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until set and refrigerate within 2 hours.
